cpp_runtime_differential_tests.scope: Counted reference suites: MSNumpress raw codecs (295), the ProForma parser (476) and writer (160), DateTime (301) and the private massDeltaText_ formatter (1078) against extracted OpenMS translation units, plus 488 predictions against unmodified external LIBSVM. Several probes substitute hand-written stub headers or a capture-only error adapter for SDK infrastructure, so the compiled unit is an adaptation rather than the shipped C++.
cpp_runtime_differential_tests.not_covered: No algorithm with SDK dependency closure -- no smoother, picker, aligner, inference algorithm or feature finder -- has been compared against executed C++. The full C++ SDK was not built. Evidence for those groups is transcribed class-test literals, independently derived expectations and Rust-only invariant tests, which detect transcription drift but not a misread algorithm.
cpp_runtime_differential_tests.harness: No full-SDK differential harness yet. Isolated probe drivers and retained outputs are recorded in per-group manifests; the prebuilt C++ reference remains outside this repository.
cpp_runtime_differential_tests.additional_probes: The FORMAT numeric-overload, SQLite S0 connector, S1 SWATH and S1 short-array Numpress probes are retained separately in their manifests, outside the scientific case totals above. Connector/SWATH contexts use declared adaptations; the short-array probe compiles the exact standalone raw codec. None executes the full SDK.

optional_json_dependency.purpose: Bounded MODOMICS JSON reader with lexical object-key iteration and correctly rounded binary64 parsing
optional_json_dependency.not_required_for: Embedded RNA registry, in-memory records and TSV loading

implemented: Owned DigestionEnzymeRNA records and RNaseDB with source alias/index replacement behavior
All fourteen source RNA enzyme definitions, registered per-code predicates and comma-composed/literal searches
RNaseDigestion sequence digestion, half-open positions and atomic output replacement
Registry-aware and default IdentificationData batch digestion: inclusive parent matches, raw-code flanks, chemical product merging and current processing history
rnase.default_difference: Native default is fully configured RNase_T1; the C++ inherited default leaves RNA-specific gains uninitialized until setEnzyme.
rnase.source_conventions: Raw record-code matching, start-first then missed-cleavage order, original outer termini and source internal-gain rewriting/overwriting; main regex is compiled against the same native subset even though RNA digestion does not use it.
rnase.limit_policy: Public digestion max fields can lower hard ceilings. Work includes tree-key comparison bounds, predicates, planning, validation and copies; output payload is measured by fragment residues plus conservative ends/context. Cut/prefix scratch is additionally bounded by the hard residue ceiling.
rnase.graph_bounds: One atomic transaction; input traversal, parsing, residue/product counts and retained payload share cumulative allowances across every parent. Parsing payload is charged before vector reservation. Graph staging and registration share separate GraphLimits.

implemented: Atomic fixed replacement
Variable variant return and atomic append with exact source subset/alternative order
modifications.candidate_identity: Caller slice order; repeated Arc allocation identities collapse, while separate equal-value allocations and same-code different chemistry remain distinct alternatives and may produce duplicate values.
modifications.source_conventions: First fixed terminal candidate and last fixed matching residue candidate win. Maximum one ignores candidate term specificity and replaces ordinary residues; the general path includes empty terminal slots independently of origin. Empty-sequence behavior is retained.
modifications.limit_policy: Configured output count/logical payload includes existing append entries even on no-op calls; checked weighted-subset preflight precedes combinatorial cloning, and staging preserves atomicity. No output deduplication or truncation.

implemented: All nine source ion series and configured intensities
Atomic single-spectrum append with signed charge range
Cumulative multiple-spectrum generation with source precursor/charge distinctions
IonNames and signed Charges annotation arrays with stable aligned sorting
spectra.source_conventions: Declared nucleoside masses, sulfur linkage corrections and a-B ambiguity behavior are preserved; source single/multiple charge progression and final-only precursor quirks remain distinct.
spectra.shared_formula_budget: Formula-based precursor fallback consumes the same remaining work and byte counters through NASequence::mono_mass_with_budget; consumed counters are retained on success and error.
spectra.metadata_policy: Unrelated destination metadata is retained in place. Peak/array staging, shape/value checks and explicit unsupported-array errors prevent partial append or silent annotation loss.

target_sdk.historical_reference_policy: Historical fixture revisions and hashes remain unchanged. Carried references use target hashes; changed source bytes record original hashes and explicit behavior reviews. Current-source manifests separately record target_verification. External Boost headers are outside this SDK comparison.

Applied processing scores, history and parent-match value semantics
Owned parent, peptide and oligo registration with stable graph-specific typed IDs
Checked graph merge and copy with reference translation
Source inclusive coverage and registry-aware RNA/peptide parent parsing
Both RNase IdentificationData digestion operations with whole-call rollback
Typed peptide fragment formula dispatch
Observation, compound, adduct, molecule and observation-match records, queries and translated graph ownership
Parent and observation-match groups with translated graph ownership
Legacy sequence import and parent-evidence export

native_boundaries: Deterministic owned IDs replace pointer ordering; foreign/stale IDs rejected
ParentMatch unknown positions use None rather than an unsigned sentinel
Unset processing timestamps use None rather than implicit system time
Atomic failure preserves existing records; resource ceilings bound cumulative work and logical payload

external_reference_note: Executed C++ oracle artifacts of the early-TOPP bundle, registered at integration. They live outside this repository under ../oracle/, so no C++ enters it; each sha256 was recomputed from the file at registration and equals the hash in the group manifest named by origin_key, which records the oracle's full artifact list. Wave 1 (2026-09-14): A1-PTE-FAIMS (../oracle/pte-faims-helper), CLI-1 (../oracle/topp-cli-lifecycle) and A2-TEXTFMT (../oracle/file-info-text-format and ../oracle/text-format) were registered at the final wave-1 merge, after their fix rounds had changed those files. The A2 group manifest tests/data/file_info_text_format_provenance.json is indexed only through origin_key: its fixtures are constants embedded in tests/file_info_text_format.rs, not files, and its target_verification has no source_revisions or source_changes, so it lacks the current_sdk_reference_manifests shape that tools/check_core_sdk.py verifies. Wave 2 (2026-09-14): P1-PICKER-LIB, A4-FILEINFO-CORE, B8-IMSPLIT and B9-OVERLAP (fix round) have that shape and are also listed in current_sdk_reference_manifests. B3-LM, P2-MZML-LENIENCY and B6-FFAP-SEEDS are indexed only through origin_key, because their target_verification records verification commands or results rather than the revision, source_revisions and source_changes the checker reads; B6's group manifest also has no external_reference_note. CLI-2 updates two CLI-1 rows (ini_read_failures.sh and its manifest, now 15 cases) and adds its own 34-case manifest, driver and rerun manifest. C1 (../oracle/topp-early-bundle) and C2 (../oracle/featurefinder-picked), which A4, B3, B6, B8 and B9 cite, are registered at W4.4. Wave 4 (2026-09-16): fix/map-normalizer's ../oracle/map-normalizer-divergence is registered here for the first time -- ten artifacts, four of them executed drivers and their logs on dax, which are the evidence behind CPP-308 and behind the closed ~13x normalisation divergence. C2 (../oracle/featurefinder-picked) is registered in the same pass: the note above said it was registered at W4.4 and it was not, so the eight artifacts tests/data/feature_finder_picked_provenance.json cites are added now. Every sha256 in this key, the 107 carried forward and the 18 added, was recomputed from the file at this integration and equals the hash in the group manifest named by origin_key; 0 mismatched and 0 were missing. The other directories these wave-4 lanes cite (../oracle/picked-chromatogram, mzml-reader-scale, topp-peak-picker-scale, baseline-filter-edges, lm-eigen-path, gauss-trace-fitter including solver-gap, b7-ffap-features, tool-threads, mzml-writer-scale-parity and topp-early-bundle) were already registered in waves 1 to 3 and were re-verified unchanged rather than re-registered. The wave-4 performance lanes archived their own callgrind profiles, A/B logs and build recipes on Ceph under /ceph/ibmi/abi/oliver/bench/openms4/results/2026-09-15-* and node-local under /scratch; those are measurement evidence, not differential oracles, and are cited by path in the support documents rather than hashed here.
